articles.title: Câmara aprova criação de marco nacional da educação em tempo integral | G1
articles.standfirst: Projeto prevê mínimo de 7 horas diárias na escola. Adoção do período integral deverá ser feita progressivamente, conforme cronograma estabelecido por cada sistema de ensino. Texto segue para análise do Senado.
articles.summary: Projeto prevê mínimo de 7 horas diárias na escola. Adoção do período integral deverá ser feita progressivamente, conforme cronograma estabelecido por cada sistema de ensino. Texto segue para análise do Senado.
articles.body:
A Câmara dos Deputados aprovou nesta quarta-feira (25) projeto de lei que cria o Marco Nacional da Educação em Tempo Integral, com, no mínimo, 7 horas diárias dos alunos nas escolas ou 35 horas semanais.

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

🏫A adoção do período integral deverá ser feita progressivamente, conforme um cronograma estabelecido por cada sistema de ensino.

O projeto, de autoria do deputado João Daniel (PT-SE), tramita na Câmara desde 2015 e foi analisado em conjunto com mais de 60 propostas similares apensadas a ele. O projeto segue agora para análise do Senado.

A coordenação nacional da política ficará a cargo do governo federal, que fará o monitoramento da sua aplicação em todo o país. Os Estados atuarão no apoio aos municípios, com suporte técnico ou financeiro.

A implementação, o planejamento e o acompanhamento da oferta do ensino em tempo integral em suas redes de ensino ficarão a cargo dos municípios e do Distrito Federal.

O planejamento deverá, obrigatoriamente, mapear:

a demanda atual e projetada dos estudantes;

as metas por etapa, modalidade e território;

os critérios de priorização e de equidade entre os estudantes - de acordo com suas vulnerabilidades;

as necessidades de infraestrutura, acessibilidade, alimentação, transporte, segurança e conectividade;

as necessidades dos profissionais da educação;

a estimativa de custos e as fontes de financiamento;

o cronograma para a implementação do ensino integral;

os indicadores de acompanhamento e avaliação que serão utilizados.

Para o planejamento, deverão participar, além dos municípios, as unidades escolares, os conselhos de educação, os professores e estudantes de cada etapa de ensino, bem como as famílias e a comunidade.

📚O projeto estabelece que a ampliação da jornada não cria, necessariamente, novos componentes curriculares obrigatórios . Isso porque também farão parte da jornada períodos para alimentação, higiene, descanso e para a convivência entre os estudantes.

O marco determina que os currículos da educação em tempo integral considerem trabalhos voltados também para os aspectos físicos e socioemocionais dos estudantes , considerando sua firmação integral e a "construção dos seus projetos de vida".

Já para os estudantes dos anos finais do Ensino Fundamental, a diretriz determina que a organização das atividades deverá se voltar para o protagonismo dos estudantes, permitindo, inclusive, que eles façam a escolha das disciplinas optativas que irão cursar, de acordo com o que for ofertado em cada escola.

Para as escolas indígenas e quilombolas, o novo currículo deverá observar suas diretrizes curriculares específicas, suas formas de organização, território, línguas e culturas.

O governo federal deverá divulgar, a cada dois anos, os resultados do monitoramento do marco. A cada quatro anos, o marco deverá ser reavaliado, com análise do cumprimento dos seus objetivos, resultados e necessidades de aperfeiçoamento.

Sala de aula vazia em Santa Catarina — Foto: Cristiano Estrela/Secom/Divulgação

A medida é uma das prioridades da frente parlamentar da educação no Congresso, que articulou a votação na Câmara e quer manter a mobilização para a pauta avançar no Senado.

O relator da proposta, deputado Thiago de Joaldo (Republicanos-SE), disse que o marco estabelece critérios para a efetividade do aumento da jornada na melhora dos níveis educacionais.

"Ampliar a jornada escolar, por si só, não é oferecer educação integral. É preciso garantir que esse tempo adicional se traduza em mais aprendizagem, mais oportunidades e desenvolvimento", disse.

articles.title: Lula sonda Haddad; Trabuco ganha força para o Ministério da Fazenda | G1
articles.standfirst: Em conversa com o presidente, Haddad desaconselhou a criação de nova pasta e reafirmou o desejo de voltar a dar aulas na USP. Próximo de Lula, Trabuco ganha força para a Fazenda em meio à insatisfação do presidente com as reações do mercado.
articles.summary: Fernando Haddad recusa cargo para voltar a dar aulas na USP, enquanto Luiz Carlos Trabuco, do Bradesco, ganha força para assumir o Ministério da Fazenda de Lula.
articles.body:
Lula e Haddad — Foto: Evaristo Sa / AFP via Getty Images

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

No encontro de ontem entre Lula e Haddad, o presidente mencionou o interesse em criar uma secretaria especial para Investimentos, vinculada à Presidência da República, com status de ministério. A nova pasta, segundo aliados de Lula, seria para abrigar Haddad no governo.

Segundo fontes a par da reunião, Haddad desaconselhou Lula a criar esse novo ministério, com o argumento de que esvaziaria as duas principais pastas do governo, a Fazenda e a Casa Civil.

Haddad defendeu a necessidade de que essas duas pastas atuem alinhadas, o que não aconteceu no Lula 3 com Haddad, que foi bombardeado pela Casa Civil.

Foram duas horas de conversa. Falaram de diversos assuntos, como política econômica, ajuste fiscal, futuro ministro da Fazenda, entre outros temas. Não foi uma discussão para tratar de cargos para Haddad no governo, mas isso acabou surgindo na conversa. Até porque era um tema incontornável.

Haddad falou a Lula que não tinha intenção de ter cargo no governo. Que o desejo dele era voltar a dar aulas na Universidade de São Paulo (USP). Lula não chegou a oferecer cargos. Em dado momento da conversa, o presidente citou a vontade de criar aquela secretaria extraordinária de investimentos estratégicos.

A avaliação de fontes do PT é que Haddad, ao dizer que não fará parte do governo, deu força para que Camilo assuma a Casa Civil, pasta que, na visão de aliados, seria a ideal para o próprio Haddad. Mas desde o final da campanha Lula tem sinalizado que Camilo deve ficar com o cargo.

Luiz Carlos Trabuco durante o Fórum Econômico Mundial em São Paulo — Foto: Paulo Whitaker/Reuters

Na montagem do novo governo, ganhou força nos bastidores o nome do presidente do Conselho de Administração do Bradesco, Luiz Carlos Trabuco, para ocupar a Fazenda. Ele e Lula se encontraram fora da agenda no Palácio da Alvorada na segunda-feira. A informação foi dada na coluna de Igor Gadelha, do Metrópoles, e o blog confirmou que o nome de Trabuco se fortaleceu.

Trabuco é um dos nomes do mercado financeiro com quem Lula tem maior proximidade. O presidente tem reclamado da reação do mercado diante da demora em escolher os nomes da nova equipe econômica e da reação dos investidores ao ajuste proposto no Plano Moretti.

Aliados de Lula afirmam que o presidente também queria ouvir Trabuco sobre a conjuntura. O governador reeleito do Piauí, Rafael Fonteles, e o vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin seguem entre as possibilidades. Bruno Moretti pode permanecer no Planejamento.

Há duas semanas, Lula se encontrou com outros economistas no Alvorada, com visão mais heterodoxa da economia, como Luciano Coutinho e Guido Mantega.

articles.title: Gustavo Gayer é denunciado pela PGR ao STF por desvio de verba | G1
articles.standfirst: Procuradoria acusa Gayer de associação criminosa, peculato e uso de documento falso. PGR diz que foi montada uma arquitetura com "múltiplos mecanismos de desvios de verbas públicas".
articles.summary: Gustavo Gayer é alvo de denúncia da PGR ao STF por peculato e uso de documento falso em esquema de desvio de cota parlamentar e uso de assessores em negócios privados.
articles.body:
A Procuradoria-Geral da República denunciou ao Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) o deputado Gustavo Gayer (PL-GO) como líder de um esquema de desvio de verba da chamada cota parlamentar . Gayer foi eleito senador em outubro para um mandato de oito anos a partir de fevereiro de 2027.

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

A Procuradoria acusa o deputado de associação criminosa, peculato e uso de documento falso.

Agora, o relator, ministro Alexandre de Moraes, vai abrir prazo para que os acusados apresentem defesa. Depois, o caso deve ser levado para julgamento na Primeira Turma do STF, que vai decidir se os denunciados serão réus e passam a responder pelos crimes.

A PGR afirmou que reuniu indícios de que Gayer:

determinou a contratação simulada da empresa de fachada;

usou equipe de gabinete para gestão de seus negócios comerciais privados;

usou imóvel alugado com recursos da Câmara dos Deputados, em Goiânia/GO, para sediar sua escola particular de idiomas e o estoque de sua loja;

aquisição fraudulenta, com seus próprios recursos, do CNPJ da associação privada ASCOMPECO/IDISE, mantida sob a gestão de "laranjas".

A Procuradoria afirmou que foi montada uma arquitetura com "múltiplos mecanismos de desvios de verbas públicas", evidenciando uma associação criminosa estável e permanente constituída com o propósito de satisfazer interesses pessoais e econômicos do grupo gravitante em torno do Deputado Federal Gustavo Gayer Machado de Araújo".

"A associação se estruturou a partir do mandato eletivo do parlamentar, o qual arregimentou e articulou assessores formais, colaboradores informais, profissionais técnicos e parentes para a execução contínua de um estratagema criminoso multipartite", diz a denúncia.

Deputado Gustavo Gayer (PL - GO) — Foto: Reprodução/Câmara dos Deputados

Além do deputado, a Procuradoria denunciou 24 pessoas entre assessores e aliados.

A PGR cita que entre os meses de março e maio de 2023 foi desviado o montante de R$ 24 mil proveniente de Cota Parlamentar vinculada ao mandato do Deputado Federal, para custear a contratação irregular de secretário parlamentar, com emissão de notas falsas.

A denúncia aponta ainda que, entre os meses de fevereiro de 2023 e janeiro de 2025, foram desviados valores mensais que variaram entre R$ 6.000,00 e R$ 6.500,00 para custeio de imóvel utilizado para fins particulares.

A investigação começou a partir da apreensão do celular de João Paulo de Sousa Cavalcante, ex-assessor de Gayer e que foi condenado pelos atos antidemocráticos de 8 de janeiro de 2023. Os dados, segundo a PGR, revelaram a simulação de contrato para pagamento com recursos vinculados ao gabinete parlamentar.

"Nesse meio tempo, João Paulo de Sousa Cavalcante executou atividades absolutamente diversas daquelas para as quais sua empresa havia sido contratada, apresentando-se, em diversos registros de conversas no aplicativo Whatsapp, como 'assessor parlamentar' do Deputado Federal – cargo, relembre-se, para o qual não satisfazia os requisitos normativos exigidos, além de perceber remuneração por fonte de recursos outra, a saber, a verba de gabinete".

articles.title: Quem é Luiz Trabuco, executivo do Bradesco cotado para ministério | G1
articles.standfirst: Executivo de carreira do Bradesco tem bom trânsito com o PT, recusou convite de Dilma em 2014 e surge como ponte entre o Palácio do Planalto e a Faria Lima em meio a tensões sobre juros e ajuste fiscal.
articles.summary: Luiz Trabuco, do Bradesco, surge como nome forte para o Ministério da Fazenda após reunião com Lula para tentar reduzir as tensões com o mercado financeiro. Veja quem é o executivo
articles.body:
Luiz Carlos Trabuco durante o Fórum Econômico Mundial em São Paulo — Foto: Paulo Whitaker/Reuters

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

O nome de Luiz Carlos Trabuco ganhou força nesta quarta-feira (25) como um dos cotados para assumir o Ministério da Fazenda, após o executivo do Bradesco ter se reunido com o presidente Lula (PT) na segunda-feira (23), fora da agenda, em Brasília.

Presidente do Conselho de Administração do banco, Trabuco é um dos nomes do mercado financeiro com quem Lula tem maior proximidade.

Desde 2023, o executivo é membro do Conselho de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social Sustentável, o Conselhão, um fórum de caráter consultivo do governo que reúne empresários, executivos, acadêmicos e representantes da sociedade civil. Lula costuma recorrer a esse grupo para discutir a conjuntura político-econômica e manter aberto o diálogo com os setores nele representados.

Na primeira reunião do Conselhão, em 2023, o executivo criticou o patamar de 13,65% da taxa de juros aplicada à época, em meio à presidência de Roberto Campos Neto no Banco Central.

Trabuco pediu "paciência" para críticos da política fiscal do governo e disse que a medida era "proibitiva".

"O custo de capital é elevadíssimo, chega a ser proibitivo para a indústria, para o comércio, para agronegócios e para os consumidores. Não se trata de esperar pelas condições macroeconômicas ótimas e ideais para um ponto de partida. Nós não podemos ser reféns de dogmas", disse.

Essa não é a primeira vez que o nome de Trabuco aparece como candidato a ministro. Em 2014, ele foi sondado pela então presidente Dilma Rousseff , mas declinou. Depois, apadrinhou a indicação de Joaquim Levy, que trabalhou sob seu comando como diretor da Bradesco Asset Management.

À época, o presidente do Bradesco elogiou a escolha, que, segundo ele, demonstrava "o compromisso do governo com o desenvolvimento, a estabilidade e a gestão competente da política econômica, numa transição sem sobressaltos".

Levy durou menos de um ano no cargo e enfrentou forte oposição do PT, que criticava os planos do governo Dilma 2 para cortar gastos e arrumar as contas públicas.

O então ministro deixou o governo em dezembro de 2015, após uma série de derrotas em que viu desidratar seu projeto de ajuste fiscal. No ano seguinte, num cenário que combinava recessão econômica e crise política, Dilma sofreu impeachment e foi substituída por Michel Temer (MDB).

Luiz Carlos Trabuco Cappi tem 75 anos e construiu uma trajetória de mais de quatro décadas no Bradesco.

De acordo com um perfil oficial do executivo na página da instituição, o executivo ingressou no banco aos 17 anos como escriturário e percorreu todos os degraus da carreira.

Ocupou postos estratégicos no banco, como diretor de Marketing, diretor-presidente da Bradesco Vida e Previdência e presidente da Bradesco Seguros.

Em 2009, foi nomeado presidente executivo (CEO) do Bradesco. À época, uma reportagem do Jornal do Brasil citou a formação do executivo em filosofia eo perfil inusitado de "um filósofo na presidência de um banco". À época, gestores ouvidos pela publicação diziam que Trabuco "entende de pessoas, produtos e números".

Em 2018, o executivo assumiu a presidência do Conselho de Administração da instituição, cargo em que permanece até hoje.

Cabe ao Conselho de Administração definir a estratégia da empresa, revisar planos e políticas de negócios, proteger os interesses dos acionistas e a supervisionar a Diretoria Executiva, assegurando a conduta ética em todas as atividades.

A gestão de Trabuco à frente do banco ficou marcada por grandes operações corporativas, incluindo a aquisição do HSBC Brasil em 2015.

Graduado em Filosofia e pós-graduado em Sócio-Psicologia pela Fundação Escola de Sociologia e Política de São Paulo (FESPSP), Trabuco também presidiu a Federação Brasileira de Bancos (Febraban), a Federação Nacional da Saúde Suplementar (Fenasaúde), a Confederação Nacional das Instituições Financeiras (CNF) e a Associação Brasileira das Entidades de Crédito Imobiliário e Poupança (Abecip).

Neste mês, assumiu a presidência do Conselho Superior do Movimento Brasil Competitivo (MBC), uma organização empresarial.

Os rumores sobre o possível convite a Trabuco vêm num momento de pressão do mercado financeiro por ajustes nas contas públicas e expectativas sobre quem será o ministro. O cenário de incertezas, somado a fatores externos, fez o dólar subir para perto de R$ 6.

Lula, por sua vez, tem criticado o mercado financeiro e afirma que não deixará a Faria Lima ditar os rumos de seu governo.

Nesta semana, após aprovação do Congresso, o presidente sancionou a lei do chamado Plano Moretti , que altera regras sobre gastos do governo e prevê gerar uma economia de até R$ 56 bilhões em 2027.

Vencida essa fase, fontes do governo afirmam que uma nova proposta com medidas fiscais alternativas começou a ser elaborada , mas a definição sobre quem será o responsável por conduzir a política econômica no governo Lula 4 segue pendente.

articles.title: GOP senator calls for vote on pro-labor bill
articles.summary: Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) is urging Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.), his Republican colleague and chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, to move forward on a union-friendly bill that would speed up first contracts for new labor unions. Hawley said in a statement Wednesday that he had previously received a commitment from…
articles.body:
Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) is urging Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.), his Republican colleague and chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, to move forward on a union-friendly bill that would speed up first contracts for new labor unions.

Hawley said in a statement Wednesday that he had previously received a commitment from Cassidy “that a vote on his legislation would occur before the end of this Congress.” Hawley is now calling on Cassidy to schedule that vote.

“We need real labor reform that puts workers first. For too long, mega corporations have denied workers’ rights and refused to meet them in good faith at the bargaining table,” Hawley said in the statement. “Now it is time for Chairman Cassidy to keep his promise to me that the Faster Labor Contracts Act receives a vote in committee before the end of the year. I fully expect the Chairman to honor his word.”

Cassidy, meanwhile, threw cold water on it. The chairman said in a statement to The Hill that he has attempted to resolve some substantive issues on the bill, which he disagrees with, with Hawley in order to give it a chance. “My staff and I have attempted on numerous occasions to address the bill’s core implementation, constitutional, and conscience issues,” Cassidy said. “We have been committed to conducting a committee process in good faith, even if ultimately on a bill I don’t support. Despite numerous attempts to engage with Senator Hawley and his staff—I texted him several times today—to resolve outstanding issues, there has been no interest in addressing problems with the legislation.”

“Senator Hawley’s press release suggests that there is greater interest in a messaging bill than in developing sound legislation. I don’t run a committee to churn out messaging bills,” he added.

Hawley is an original co-sponsor of the bill, along with Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) and Democratic Sens. Cory Booker (N.J.), Jeff Merkley (Ore.) and Gary Peters (Mich.).

Hawley, who has garnered some attention as a potential 2028 presidential contender, is also a vocal advocate for labor unions in the Republican Party, which traditionally sides with business and industry leaders over unions.

The legislation would authorize government arbitrators to get involved if new unions can’t find agreement with employers within 120 days, preventing employers from stalling negotiations. It has backing from the Teamsters, one of the largest U.S. labor unions.

But the bill moving forward is a red flag for the business community, whch generally supports Republican policies.

The U.S. Chamber of Commerce sent a strongly worded letter opposing the bill in June when the House passed it, arguing it creates an unrealistic timeline that will result in the government negotiating contracts.

“The U.S. Chamber of Commerce strongly opposes the Faster Labor Contracts Act (H.R. 5408), a proposal that could take away workers’ right to vote on the terms and conditions of their own employment by replacing negotiation with forced, government-written contracts,” said Rodney Davis, senior vice president for government affairs, in the letter at the time.

articles.title: Trump: Iowa Gov.-elect Sand was ‘absolutely no help’ in controlled lead blast
articles.summary: President Trump criticized Iowa Gov.-elect Rob Sand (D) in the wake of the controlled lead blast in the state Wednesday, accusing the incoming governor of hurting the process. “Rob, the new future Governor of Iowa, is obviously unhappy that the Obama created (2009!) mess was so perfectly handled by the U.S. Army through a flawless…
articles.body:
President Trump criticized Iowa Gov.-elect Rob Sand (D) in the wake of the controlled lead blast in the state Wednesday, accusing the incoming governor of hurting the process.

“Rob, the new future Governor of Iowa, is obviously unhappy that the Obama created (2009!) mess was so perfectly handled by the U.S. Army through a flawless detonation, that he’s now complaining about the lead up to the event,” Trump wrote in a Wednesday afternoon post to Truth Social.

“He hurt and delayed the process. Was absolutely no help. Just another politician. He should rejoice at this great success, not nitpick and issue phony complaints on ‘transparency.’ I will remember!” the president continued.

The Army detonated a cache of degraded lead-based munitions in Iowa on Wednesday morning to prevent an accidental explosion, which could have caused toxic particles to spread through the air uncontrollably.

However, Trump’s newly appointed chief of staff and longtime ally, Stephen Miller, thanked Sand — along with outgoing Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds (R) and other state and federal officials — for their cooperative efforts in a post on the social platform X following the blast.

Critics have raised concerns over how the situation was able to escalate to the point where lead azide-containing weapons were at risk of exploding.

Locals residing close to the site and public health experts also said prior to the controlled detonation they feared the potential lead exposure could have adverse effects on community members — especially children — as well as livestock

articles.title: Trump's birthright citizenship restrictions struck down again by DC federal judge he called 'hater'
articles.summary: Judge Christopher Cooper struck down Trump's second birthright citizenship order, citing the Fourteenth Amendment and rejecting surrogacy-based exclusions.
articles.body: A DC federal judge, previously dubbed by President Donald Trump as an "anti- Trump Hater," blocked Trump's second attempt to restrict birthright citizenship in a Wednesday ruling. U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper, who was recently in Trump's crosshairs after ruling against efforts to shut down the Kennedy Center for renovations and add Trump's name to the cultural institution, issued a 67-page ruling striking down an August executive order that barred U.S. -born children whose parents are suspected terrorists or gang members, or children born through surrogacy to foreign parents, from citizenship eligibility. Cooper's ruling comes months after the Supreme Court struck down Trump's initial executive order, signed on his first day back in office. The order attempted to deny birthright citizenship to U.S.-born children whose mothers were in the country illegally or temporarily and whose fathers were neither U.S. citizens nor green card holders. WHITE HOUSE RIPS ‘ACTIVIST’ BIDEN JUDGE WHO UPENDED TRUMP BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP ORDER "As the Supreme Court has made clear, however, the President cannot carve out new exceptions to birthright citizenship for children born within the United States and subject to its laws," Cooper ruled. Trump's second executive order was already partially blocked on Sept. 2 by U.S. District Judge Deborah Boardman in Maryland, whose injunction protected U.S.-born children of mothers who were in the country illegally or temporarily and whose fathers were neither U.S. citizens nor lawful permanent residents. Cooper's ruling expanded protections beyond that class to include additional children born to certain foreign government and international organization employees, parents deemed "alien enemies" by the administration and foreign parents who used commercial surrogacy services in the U.S. "The merits in this case are clear-cut. The Supreme Court has twice confirmed that all children born in this country are U.S. citizens, save only for the small handful who are not subject to U.S. law," Cooper wrote. In addition to the Supreme Court's June ruling in Trump v. Barbara, Cooper referred to the high court's ruling in United States v. Wong Kim Ark, which determined that a man born to Chinese immigrants was a protected U.S. citizen under the 14th Amendment. SEN ERIC SCHMITT SEEKS TO END BIRTH TOURISM, REVOKE CITIZENSHIP FOR BABIES OF FOREIGN DIPLOMATS Cooper noted that Wong Kim Ark established narrow exceptions to birthright citizenship, including for children of foreign diplomats, children born aboard foreign public ships and children of enemy forces occupying American territory. "While the Fourteenth Amendment may theoretically permit new exceptions beyond those listed in Wong Kim Ark, Congress has not authorized any such exceptions," Cooper wrote. Cooper argued that membership in a terrorist organization alone does not satisfy the historical exception to birthright citizenship for children of enemy forces occupying U.S. territory. He criticized the Trump administration's contention that foreign invaders could occupy American territory without actually holding it as an "outside-the-box understanding" of what constitutes an occupation. "To recap, a parent’s purported status as an alien enemy, standing alone, cannot strip a U.S.-born child of his right to birthright citizenship," Cooper wrote. "The alien-enemy exception, properly understood, applies only to children born to hostile enemy forces in temporarily occupied U.S. territory." Cooper also rejected Trump's attempt to deny birthright citizenship to children born through commercial surrogacy arrangements involving foreign parents, finding that the circumstances of their birth do not exempt them from U.S. jurisdiction. "Indeed, foreign parents choose surrogacy arrangements in the United States precisely to have the child be governed by U.S. law and have the surrogacy process ‘supervised by a court.," Cooper wrote. TRUMP TO ASK SUPREME COURT TO REHEAR BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP CASE AFTER 'INSANE DECISION' He noted that, prior to Trump's second executive order, the State Department recognized the citizenship of children born on American soil regardless of whether they were born through surrogacy. The Trump administration is expected to appeal the decision and request that the executive order be temporarily enforced while the litigation works its way through the courts, a process that could take months. "This is just another ruling from an activist judge appointed by Obama attempting to thwart President Trump’s commonsense agenda," White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "The birthright citizenship executive order is consistent with the holdings and analysis set forth by the Supreme Court." The Justice Department could seek temporary relief from the U.S. Court of Appeals for the DC Circuit or seek intervention from the Supreme Court. Fox News Digital reached out to the Justice Department for comment. articles.body:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) on Tuesday arrested a Salvadoran man a week after he won $1 million playing the Massachusetts Lottery.

ICE’s Boston office wrote in a statement on social media that officers arrested Ariel Antonio Velasquez-Morales in east Boston, after what Fox News reported was a “brief foot chase.” He entered the country in 2013, and an immigration judge ordered his removal the following year.

The statement included a photo of Velasquez-Morales after he received his oversized check from the Massachusetts Lottery’s headquarters in Dorchester, a Boston neighborhood. The agency said him winning the lottery prize led to his arrest.

Velasquez-Morales won from the “$2,000,000 50X Cashword” crossword-style scratch ticket game, with his name appearing on the check as “Ariel Velasquez.”

“Welcome to the ERO Boston lottery! Where illegal aliens and sanctuary politicians are out of luck, and the law-abiding citizens of New England are always the winners!” the Boston ICE office stated .

The agency said in a separate statement that the “rights and privileges reserved for American citizens are for American citizens, NOT illegal aliens. The patriots of ICE continue to work around the clock to enforce our nation’s laws and serve the American people.”

Research from the University of Michigan in 2009 showed that 43.9 percent of immigrants without permanent legal status, out of a sampling of 431 respondents, play scratch-and-win tickets or the lottery.

The incident came on the day that Salvadoran migrant Kilmar Abrego Garcia self-deported following a protracted legal battle to remain in the U.S. after he was deported last year and then faced charges in connection with human smuggling claims made by the Department of Justice (DOJ).

Abrego Garcia, previously a Maryland resident, arrived in Madrid on Wednesday and raised a fist as he entered a van, not speaking to reporters, according to The Associated Press . His ICE ankle monitor was removed following his departure, CBS News reported .

“I want to share my joy. I feel happy because I can breathe. I feel free — free of everything evil that I’ve been through and I can breathe freedom,” he said in Spanish on a call with reporters .

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin wrote on the social platform X that his department was “delighted” that Abrego Garcia self-deported and said he “will no longer terrorize innocent Americans.”

Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), who met with Abrego Garcia in El Salvador after he was deported last year and sent to the Salvadoran megaprison CECOT, said he was “relieved” that Abrego Garcia “will be safe.”

articles.title: Bottoms to be inaugurated at Atlanta’s State Farm Arena
articles.summary: Georgia Gov.-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms (D) will be sworn into office on Jan. 12, her transition team announced Wednesday, marking the first time in U.S. history that a Black woman will serve as governor. The former Atlanta mayor will take the oath of office as Georgia’s 84th governor at 11 a.m. at State Farm Arena…
articles.body:
Georgia Gov.-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms (D) will be sworn into office on Jan. 12, her transition team announced Wednesday, marking the first time in U.S. history that a Black woman will serve as governor.

The former Atlanta mayor will take the oath of office as Georgia’s 84th governor at 11 a.m. at State Farm Arena in downtown Atlanta, home of the NBA’s Atlanta Hawks. Lt. Gov.-elect Josh McLaurin (D) and Georgia’s other statewide constitutional officers will also be sworn in during the ceremony.

“Due to the tremendous interest in this event, we will host the inauguration at State Farm Arena to enable Georgians from across the state to participate in the ceremony,” transition chief of staff Tharon Johnson said in a release.

Johnson continued, “Ahead of inauguration, Governor-Elect Bottoms is working with her transition team to hit the ground running on day one with an agenda focused on lowering costs, creating opportunity and building a stronger future for every Georgia community.”

Bottoms, who served as Atlanta’s mayor from 2018 to 2022 and later as a senior adviser in the Biden administration, has assembled a transition team that includes several prominent Georgia business and entertainment figures.

Media mogul Tyler Perry is serving as a co-chair of the transition effort, dubbed “Georgia’s Promise.” Home Depot co-founder Arthur Blank and former Walgreens CEO Rosalind Brewer are also among its members.

Bottoms defeated Republican healthcare executive Rick Jackson by more than 8 percentage points during the midterm elections earlier this month, according to Decision Desk HQ .

She will succeed term-limited Gov. Brian Kemp (R), becoming Georgia’s first Democratic governor since Roy Barnes left office in 2003. She will also be the first woman and first Black person to hold the office in the state.

Her transition team said additional information about the inauguration, including how to obtain tickets and plans for an inaugural ball, will be released in the coming weeks.

articles.title: Sherrill declares state of emergency as Thanksgiving storm approaches
articles.summary: New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill (D) declared a state of emergency Wednesday as a nor’easter moved up the East Coast, bringing heavy rain and high winds and delaying thousands of flights. “Damaging winds, heavy rain, and severe tidal flooding are expected through Friday, with the most dangerous conditions on Thanksgiving Day,” Sherrill wrote on social…
articles.body:
New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill (D) declared a state of emergency Wednesday as a nor’easter moved up the East Coast, bringing heavy rain and high winds and delaying thousands of flights.

“Damaging winds, heavy rain, and severe tidal flooding are expected through Friday, with the most dangerous conditions on Thanksgiving Day,” Sherrill wrote on social platform X. “Be prepared for prolonged power outages, detours, and road closures. Please travel today if possible, charge your devices, and never drive through flooded roadways.”

The state of emergency takes effect at 6 p.m. EST Wednesday.

A major storm moved through Florida, Georgia and the Carolinas on Wednesday and will slam the Washington and New York areas with heavy rain and high winds on Thanksgiving. A separate storm moved from the Deep South to the Midwest, with the potential for several inches of snow near St. Louis.

As of Wednesday afternoon, New Jersey was the only East Coast state to have declared a state of emergency for the storm.

Sherrill said impacts will be especially pronounced in Cape May, Ocean and Atlantic counties, where coastal flooding is a threat. The governor said high winds will impact the entire state.

The National Weather Service forecast says major coastal flooding is possible near Cape May, Avalon, Ocean City and Atlantic City, N.J., and wind gusts on the Garden State’s coast will reach up to 70 miles per hour. Wind gusts away from the coast will be closer to 55-60 mph.

The storm is already upending Thanksgiving travel, delaying thousands of flights nationwide.

New Jersey’s Newark Liberty International Airport has the second most delays of any U.S. airport as of Wednesday afternoon, according to flight tracking website FlightAware, and delays continue to stack up around the country. More than 4,200 flights within, into or out of the U.S. have been delayed, though just 62 have been canceled, according to FlightAware.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Wednesday that a majority of Tuesday’s flight delays were weather-related, but projected that delays could increase as storms move up the East Coast and hit some of the nation’s busiest airports.

“Despite the massive volume, average delay time stayed around 32.4 minutes,” he wrote Wednesday on social platform X. “I recognize and sympathize with the inconvenience any lost time causes travelers who are understandably anxious to be with their families, but our top priority will always be your safety.”

The New York and New Jersey area is facing possibly the worst of the storm and Macy’s has already postponed the 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday morning due to the high winds and rain.

Authorities also noted the company engaged in a “long-running conspiracy” to steal intellectual property , including trade secret information and copyrighted works, from American companies.

articles.title: Talarico, Cruz push for Space Academy to be in Texas
articles.summary: Sen. Ted Cruz (R) and Sen.-elect James Talarico (D), who are poised to hold Texas’s two seats in the upper chamber for at least the next four years, are campaigning together in a rare bipartisan move for President Trump’s proposed U.S. Space Academy to be built in their home state. “We share a commitment to…
articles.body:
Sen. Ted Cruz (R) and Sen.-elect James Talarico (D), who are poised to hold Texas’s two seats in the upper chamber for at least the next four years, are campaigning together in a rare bipartisan move for President Trump’s proposed U.S. Space Academy to be built in their home state.

“We share a commitment to strengthening Texas’s economy and ensuring our state plays a leading role in America’s future in space,” Cruz and Talarico wrote in a joint statement . “We look forward to working together to bring this opportunity to the Lone Star State and to support the U.S. Space Academy for years to come.”

The duo cited the Lone Star State’s history as being the epicenter for the American aerospace industry, infrastructure and expertise given that it’s home to NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston.

“Texas is best suited to train the next generation of American space leaders and is the natural home for the U.S. Space Academy,” they continued.

The move would bring “tremendous opportunities” for Texans, Talarico and Cruz said, arguing the academy’s presence would create thousands of jobs, grow local businesses and expand existing partnerships with research institutions.

Trump signed an executive order in August establishing a hub for recruiting and training astronauts, engineers, scientists and other space exploration professionals, though the administration has yet to announce its location. The president noted during the order’s unveiling that Cruz was already lobbying for the academy to be housed in Texas.

Cruz said Saturday he told Talarico it “would be really powerful if we had a bipartisan commitment to fight for the Space Academy being in Texas.”

“He [Talarico] was enthusiastic; he said he was eager to work with me on that, and so we’re going to do it together,” the GOP senator continued.

Talarico made history earlier this month as the first Democratic Senate candidate to be elected in Texas in more than 30 years. Though Cruz urged voters to support Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton (R) in the Senate race, the GOP senator later called Talarico’s triumph “impressive” before offering to get coffee or tequila with the senator-elect to discuss how they could work together across party lines.

Outgoing Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas) similarly said he would be cheering Talarico on if the incoming senator did “a good job” representing Texas and pledged to do all he could to help his contemporary during the transition.

“He seems like a nice guy, and I wish him well,” Cornyn said. “He’s going to have an interesting time navigating a red state as a Democrat.”

articles.title: Blindsided by Iowa detonation, White House scrambled, sources say
articles.summary: White House officials have expressed frustration in internal conversations that they had to scramble to deal with the crisis.
articles.body:
Washington — The chaotic lead-up to Wednesday's detonation of barrels of chemicals at a U.S. Army munitions plant in Iowa that raised contamination fears has prompted questions inside the Trump administration about what went wrong and who was to blame for not elevating the matter to senior officials sooner, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.

President Trump and other administration officials praised the controlled detonation of about 5 tons of degraded lead azide at the plant in Middletown as having "exceeded expectations," saying maximum mitigation efforts were successfully achieved.

"Great job by the Army, and others, in Iowa!!! President DJT," Mr. Trump posted on Truth Social about five hours after the blast took place.

But White House officials have expressed frustration in internal conversations that they had to scramble to deal with the crisis. The situation rapidly became a national news story, with complaints from Iowa residents that they had not received sufficient notice about the potential dangers.

The Army had known since spring that the lead azide at the plant posed a threat to the public and to the environment, but then-Army Secretary Dan Driscoll failed to raise the issue to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth or to other senior administration officials, according to several U.S. officials who requested anonymity to speak about a controversial topic.

A separate source familiar with the discussions surrounding the ammunition said the Army notified Hegseth's office early on. The notification never reached Hegseth directly, other officials said.

The process of coordinating the response was triggered before Driscoll left the administration, two sources said. Driscoll resigned in September amid tensions with Hegseth.

Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle learned of the stored chemicals and the risks in September, officials told CBS News, but didn't brief superiors. There have been discussions about quietly moving Telle out of the acting role in coming weeks, several sources said.

Administration leaders at the most senior levels were taken by surprise when they learned Thursday about the extent of the problem as they flew home from China after Mr. Trump's Asia trip, one U.S. official said. That forced White House chief of staff Stephen Miller to launch an intensive response from Air Force One, involving hours of phone calls, a dozen agencies and nearly every member of the Cabinet.

Mr. Trump and other White House officials in post-blast conversations Wednesday were relieved about the results of the detonation and the steps taken from Thursday on to handle the crisis. But Mr. Trump was furious about how the Army had handled the matter in the months before that, three of the sources said.

The president's plans to golf Wednesday in West Palm Beach were dashed by rain, and he watched the television coverage of events in Iowa closely, sources told CBS News.

There have also been internal administration conversations about the role in this by Gen. Christopher LaNeve, the Army's chief of staff, the sources said.

Other officials defended the administration action, saying the dozens of lower-level career officials who knew about the impending danger from the lead azide for months appropriately discussed how to handle it.

CBS News reached out to the White House for comment. The Pentagon referred questions to the Army, which has not yet responded to a request for comment.

In March, the Army officially notified the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency that 68 barrels of potentially unstable chemicals were discovered during a routine inspection at the Iowa plant.

Vice President JD Vance told reporters Wednesday that the administration became aware about six months ago "that it was impossible to move it — it was impossible to effectively neutralize it without causing significant danger to the surrounding community." Vance said the administration examined other options.

But other U.S. officials said the conclusion was reached only about two months ago that a controlled detonation would be the only safe way to get rid of the chemicals. A private contractor retained by the Pentagon looked into potential disposal processes, two of the sources said.

Miller worked on the problem over the weekend before the blast, calling various officials, including Iowa Gov.-elect Rob Sand on Monday, two sources said. The administration sought to keep the response – and the public blame – bipartisan, one of the sources said.

Miller thanked Sand and outgoing Gov. Kim Reynolds "for their cooperation and engagement" shortly after the detonation.

Sand and Mr. Trump have exchanged some verbal blows. The Democratic governor-elect said on social media Wednesday the "lead-up to the detonation should never have been so chaotic and unclear," and called for "immediate transparency." Mr. Trump responded by writing that Sand had "hurt and delayed the process" and should stop trying to "nitpick and issue phony complaints."

Earlier in the week, Mr. Trump said the detonation wouldn't move forward unless Sand and an appeals court approved, but warned he would hold Sand responsible "for any and all death or destruction" if he blocked the operation. Sand, who did not have authority over the detonation, responded that the Trump administration should make the decision based on the information available.

A federal appeals court on Monday cleared the way for the detonation amid challenges from environmental groups and elected officials about the operation's potential risks to public health. The military ultimately went forward with a controlled blast of the material, rather than letting it further degrade.

Maps released Tuesday by the Army noted that the dust cloud may travel as far as 100 miles, but the most potent effects would likely be felt within 30 square miles of the munitions plant.

Fifteen minutes after the detonation, the Environmental Protection Agency reported that zero lead was detected in the air by four monitoring stations in the area. Those sensors continued to show the same readings two hours later, according to the EPA.

The Army said it had taken steps to barricade the concrete bunkers holding the munitions and absorb the toxic dust, including with aqueous foam, which is used to extinguish fuel fires.

articles.title: Judge halts order requiring Fulton County to turn over copies of 2020 ballots to Georgia election board
articles.summary: The judge previously ruled the county had to turn over unredacted digital copies of election materials to the State Election Board, which is run by Trump allies.
articles.body: A Fulton County judge on Wednesday paused her own order from a day before that had required the county to hand over digital copies of its 2020 election records to the Georgia State Election Board. Superior Court Judge Kelly Lee Ellerbe halted the previous day’s order while the appeal from the county plays out. The move by Ellerbe, who issued a one-page ruling that did not elaborate on her reasoning, came hours before the 5 p.m. ET deadline to hand over records to the election board, which is controlled by allies of President Donald Trump. Atlanta’s Fulton County, which is the home of a large chunk of the state’s Democratic voters, has long been a target of Trump and his allies as they seek to find evidence to support their false claims of widespread voter fraud in the 2020 election won by former President Joe Biden. The records at the heart of the Georgia case are unredacted digital copies of 2020 election materials, the originals of which were seized from the county’s elections hub in January by the FBI in an unusual federal intervention into a state-run election. The judge said Tuesday that the records could only be disclosed to a limited number of parties outlined in the order. The board has been trying to obtain the records since 2024.

articles.title: Socialists on blast for pledging to weed money out of politics but accepting business execs' checks anyway
articles.summary: An investigation of FEC records found 24 corporate executives gave $675,300 to DSA-endorsed candidates like Rashida Tlaib and progressive PACs.
articles.body: Far-left lawmakers are facing accusations of hypocrisy for criticizing corporate influence in politics while accepting campaign contributions from influential executives in industries including defense and healthcare. A new investigation looking into Federal Election Commission filings found socialist-aligned candidates who pledged to reject corporate PAC contributions still took the cash from PAC's and corporate executives. "If you're taking money from them, at least be man enough to admit you're going to take the money," Rep.-elect Jerry Carl, R-Ala., told Fox News Digital in reference to Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich. Filings first flagged by anti-DEI nonprofit 1792 Exchange were reviewed by Fox News Digital. They show Tlaib accepted checks in 2023 and 2025 totaling $10,600 from L3Harris executive defense contractor Faisal Munir, even after she authored an op-ed in 2025 criticizing lawmakers who financially benefit from the defense industry. RADICAL SOCIALIST WING'S HUGE NIGHT REVEALS ASCENDING CLOUT WITHIN DEMOCRATIC PARTY Other Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) members, such as, Reps.-elect Donavan McKinney, D-Mich., Claire Valdez, D-N.Y., and Darializa Avila Chevalier, D-N.Y., publicly pledged to reject corporate PAC contributions, according to End Citizens United. Yet all three took cash from PACs and corporate executives, as noted in the investigation. While still candidates, however, they never specified if their pledge to reject corporate money also applies to the individuals running corporations and those outside PACs. On her campaign website, Chevalier calls for banning super PAC money from elections, arguing that the political system "rewards the wealthy elite, corporations, and political machines over working people." Valdez, similarly, has criticized money in politics and blamed "AIPAC, crypto and AI" for "spending millions and millions of dollars" in "trying to influence the elections." McKinney denounced the campaign finance system on his website, arguing that it prevents elected officials from addressing voters' concerns. 'SQUAD' RAKES IN RECORD $2.35M WHILE SLAMMING THE DOOR ON COP DONATIONS Omar Tawakol, CEO of AI advertising platform Rembrand, contributed $13,600 to Tlaib, $7,000 to McKinney and $3,500 each to Valdez and Chevalier. The initial investigation notes that 24 corporate executives contributed a combined $675,300 to DSA-endorsed congressional candidates during the two previous election cycles. 17 of those 24 contributed $126,300 directly to the DSA-endorsed candidates. The other $549,000 went to three progressive political action committees: Justice Democrats, Leaders We Deserve and the Working Families Party PAC, which largely relies on money from corporate executives and other PACs which support the DSA candidates. Justice Democrats contributed to Chevalier, Tlaib and Valdez, while Leaders We Deserve supported McKinney and Valdez. The Working Families Party PAC supported McKinney. Justice Democrats received $150,000 from Desmos Studio CEO Eli Luberoff and $85,000 from Hims & Hers Health CEO Andrew Dudum. Android co-founder Rich Miner contributed $65,000 to Leaders We Deserve, while former Google chief scientist Jeff Dean donated $100,000 to the Working Families Party PAC. Heritage Foundation chief economist E.J. Antoni spelled out for Fox News Digital how executives often support candidates in hopes of securing regulatory "carve-outs, exemptions, and exclusions" if they are elected to positions where they can introduce or influence related policy in the future. The campaign finance records do not establish that any of the executives sought or received preferential treatment in exchange for their contributions. PROGRESSIVE GROUP'S 182-PAGE BLUEPRINT MAPS OUT POTENTIAL DEM INVESTIGATIONS INTO TRUMP, CORPORATE ALLIES CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Keira Havens, founder of Courage for Democracy, the organization behind President Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth impeachment efforts, told Fox News Digital that the "solution" to the "corruption" displayed by the politicians is "accountability." DSA-endorsed politicians Valdez, Chevalier, McKinney and Tlaib all did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment, neither did the DSA itself.The PACs — Justice Democrats, Working Families Party and Leaders We Deserve — also did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

articles.body:
Podcaster Joe Rogan on Wednesday blasted Republicans who lost in the 2026 midterm elections and warned them that the American people won’t “tolerate any of this stupid s— anymore.”

Rogan told podcaster and former Navy SEAL Jocko Willink on “ The Joe Rogan Experience ” that he’s told people shaken by the GOP’s sweeping losses that it is “how it’s supposed to be.”

“You can’t just want your team to win always,” he continued. “If your team does stupid things and says a bunch of things that they were gonna do but didn’t do, says they’re never gonna do that, but then they do it, you break a bunch of promises, you have a bunch of f—ing loony people that are running everything, they get corrupted, there’s a lot of f—ing chaos going on, people are supposed to vote it out.”

The podcast host later said, “Realize the American people, they’re not going to tolerate this stupid s— anymore,” that Republicans “can’t just f— everything up and expect to keep winning” and that he knew many Texas Republicans who voted for Democrats “down the line.”

“You get better candidates, you get better policies … people won’t take it anymore,” Rogan said. “They’re gonna vote you out … and then the Republicans have a chance in a few years to regroup.”

Rogan’s criticisms of the GOP and President Trump, who he endorsed in 2024 , mounted going into the midterms. He criticized Trump’s handling of the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran, saying in July that the president “ might’ve f—ed up .”

“I mean, this war is not something anybody that’s conservative wanted. Most people don’t want it, except supporters of Israel,” he said on his podcast at the time.

Rogan also vented frustration over whether the administration was delivering on the promises that helped fuel Trump’s return to the White House, specifically the Department of Justice’s handling of its documents and records connected to deceased convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

“We’re all pissed. We all thought that, you know, all that stuff was gonna be released right after the election. We’re gonna drain the swamp and find all the pedophiles,” the podcast host said in June.

Rogan’s not alone in urging Republicans to not ignore what led to their losses earlier this month.

A week after the midterms, Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.) called on his colleagues not to downplay the blowout losses. He said they should work hard to pass Trump’s agenda in the lame-duck period before Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress.

“This was not a normal midterm election loss,” Kennedy told Fox News’s Sean Hannity in an interview. “If you think that, congratulations, you’re stupid.”

articles.body:
A Fulton County, Ga., judge Wednesday blocked her own order for the county to turn over copies of ballots seized by the FBI in a raid earlier this year to the Georgia State Election Board.

Superior Court Judge Kelly Lee Ellerbe paused her order issued Tuesday after county election officials filed a notice of appeal. She issued the pause hours before the 5 p.m. EST deadline to hand the records back to the Georgia State Election Board. The appeal remains pending.

Ellerbe’s original order does not directly specify the reason the records must be turned over.

Republicans, led by President Trump, have made attempts to relitigate the 2020 election results in Georgia and specifically in Fulton County, home to most of Atlanta. Trump has claimed, without evidence, that the 2020 election in Georgia was stolen despite several recounts showing former President Biden won.

Republican state officials oversaw the 2020 election results, but they refused to overturn Biden’s win at Trump’s urging that they find more votes for him.

The FBI raided Fulton County in January, seizing 2020 election ballots as part of an investigation into alleged “irregularities,” but a judge later ruled that the government could hold on to those ballots despite Fulton County’s efforts to have them returned. No charges have been filed.

The agency deemed the Fulton County case a priority investigation and moved to allocate hundreds of agents to the investigation.

A sweeping 2021 election law stripped Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger of his authority to oversee elections, having previously chaired the State Election Board.

Former Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard’s presence during the FBI seizure raised concerns for lawmakers. She later deflected questions from Democrats on the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence after she was photographed outside of the Georgia election office during the FBI raid.

“I believe an organized effort to misuse her national security powers, to interfere in domestic politics, and potentially provide a pretext for the president’s unconstitutional efforts to seize control of the upcoming elections,” Sen. Mark Warner (D-Va.) said in his opening remarks at a hearing in March.

Gabbard resigned in May with Jay Clayton later sworn in to replace her in August. Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.) grilled Clayton during his confirmation hearing in July as he and other Democrats asked him who won the 2020 election. Clayton told Warner that Biden “was certified” as president and later told Ossoff that he was “not going to engage in the theater.”

articles.title: Mamdani will miss postponed Thanksgiving parade after Achilles surgery
articles.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) said he will miss the postponed Macy’s Thanksgiving parade Saturday because he is scheduled to receive surgery Friday on his right leg after tearing his Achilles tendon. The mayor confirmed at a press conference Wednesday that he could not attend the rescheduled event, saying he was “very disappointed…
articles.body:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) said he will miss the postponed Macy’s Thanksgiving parade Saturday because he is scheduled to receive surgery Friday on his right leg after tearing his Achilles tendon.

The mayor confirmed at a press conference Wednesday that he could not attend the rescheduled event, saying he was “very disappointed about it.”

“I’ve been looking forward to attending this parade, and now, as a result of the rescheduling, I will not be able to make it because of the doctor’s orders,” he stated.

Macy’s pushed its Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, citing a severe storm moving up the East Coast, which is forecast to bring heavy rain and wind. The parade is now scheduled for 8:30 a.m. EST Saturday. This year marks the 100th parade of the Thanksgiving Day tradition.

Mamdani injured his right leg earlier this week during a friendly soccer match against members of New York City’s press corps. He said he would be in the hospital Friday from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. EST after revealing it would be his first surgery.

“I scored a goal soon after getting on the pitch, and I forgot that I was 35,” Mamdani expressed last week. “And soon after I tore my Achilles.”

When discussing the decision to push the parade, Mamdani told reporters that he understood “this change of plans will cause inconveniences, yet safety has to come first.”

“Safety is and will always remain our top priority, and this will be a heavy storm,” he continued.

The National Weather Service (NWS) issued a high-wind warning for New York City along with a coastal flood warning from Wednesday to Thursday. It forecast winds of 25 mph to 35 mph with gusts up to 60 mph expected. For flooding, the NWS predicted 1.5 feet of inundation above ground level in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline.

Mamdani and New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch both confirmed there were “no known specific or credible threats to the parade at this time,” adding that there will be an increased police presence at Saturday’s parade.

“Thousands of officers will be deployed, supported by specialized units from across the department, including Canine, Harbor, Aviation, ESU and more,” Mamdani stated.

articles.title: Fundo Eleitoral: Repasses estão acima do valor recebido por 6 partidos | G1
articles.standfirst: Divergências dificultam o rastreamento da origem e da destinação dos recursos de campanha e comprometem, com base nos dados disponíveis, a análise da distribuição do Fundo Eleitoral para mulheres e pessoas negras. Segundo o TSE, eventuais erros serão apurados no julgamento das prestações de contas dos candidatos.
articles.summary: Levantamento aponta que o Fundo Eleitoral de 2026 tem divergências milionárias em seis partidos, prejudicando a transparência e a fiscalização de cotas raciais.
articles.body:
Fachada do TSE — Foto: Luiz Roberto/Secom/TSE

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

As prestações de contas dos candidatos nas eleições de 2026 apresentam divergências entre os valores declarados como recursos do Fundo Especial de Financiamento de Campanha (FEFC), o Fundo Eleitoral, e as quantias distribuídas aos partidos pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

Em seis partidos — PCdoB, Podemos, PP, PSD, Republicanos e União Brasil —, a soma dos valores declarados pelos candidatos como repasses do Fundo Eleitoral, feitos por diretórios nacionais, estaduais e municipais, supera o total de recursos recebidos pelas siglas.

A maior divergência foi identificada no PP, que recebeu R$ 417,07 milhões do Fundo Eleitoral, mas teve R$ 422,13 milhões declarados pelos candidatos como repasses dos diretórios partidários, uma diferença de R$ 5,06 milhões.

Em seguida aparecem União Brasil (R$ 4,36 milhões), PSD (R$ 3,16 milhões), Podemos (R$ 1,79 milhão), Republicanos (R$ 220,5 mil) e PCdoB (R$ 128 mil). No caso do PP, mesmo quando considerados apenas os repasses feitos diretamente pelo diretório nacional, o valor declarado pelos candidatos supera a quantia recebida pelo partido.

Especialistas ouvidos pelo g1 explicaram que as divergências não indicam, por si só, irregularidades. No entanto, dificultam o rastreamento da origem e do destino do dinheiro utilizado nas campanhas. Também comprometem a verificação do cumprimento das cotas mínimas de recursos do Fundo Eleitoral para candidaturas de mulheres e pessoas negras, com base nos dados disponíveis até o momento.

🔎 O Fundo Eleitoral é transferido pelo Tesouro Nacional ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), responsável por distribuir os recursos aos diretórios nacionais dos partidos. Esses diretórios podem repassar o dinheiro diretamente aos candidatos ou transferi-lo para diretórios estaduais e municipais, que, por sua vez, financiam as campanhas. A distribuição deve respeitar as regras eleitorais, incluindo as cotas mínimas de recursos para candidaturas de mulheres e pessoas negras.

🔎 A divisão dos recursos segue critérios previstos em lei e beneficia os partidos com maior representação no Congresso. Siglas sem deputados federais ou senadores recebem o valor mínimo de R$ 3,3 milhões. Em 2026, o PL ficou com a maior parcela do fundo, superior a R$ 880 milhões.

As divergências foram identificadas em levantamento do g1 com base nas receitas declaradas pelos candidatos à Justiça Eleitoral. Os dados foram extraídos do portal de dados abertos do TSE em 17 de novembro, após o fim do prazo para a entrega das prestações de contas finais das campanhas.

O levantamento considerou os repasses feitos aos candidatos por diretórios nacionais, estaduais e municipais, classificados como provenientes do Fundo Eleitoral. Foram incluídas transferências eletrônicas, PIX, cheques, depósitos em espécie, repasses em dinheiro e pagamentos de serviços com valores estimáveis em dinheiro.

Para evitar a dupla contagem de recursos, a análise incluiu apenas as receitas identificadas como "Recursos de partido político". Com isso, ficaram de fora as transferências entre candidatos, que poderiam fazer com que um mesmo valor fosse contabilizado mais de uma vez.

Segundo a advogada eleitoralista e pesquisadora Bianca Gonçalves e Silva, as inconsistências podem decorrer de erros na identificação da origem dos recursos durante o preenchimento das prestações de contas, cuja responsabilidade é de cada candidato. "O que pode acontecer aí é que o candidato coloca como sendo um repasse do Fundo Eleitoral, o pode ser do Fundo Partidário, por exemplo”, afirmou.

Os seis partidos foram procurados pelo g1 , mas apenas o PSD e o Podemos responderam, por meio da assessoria de imprensa. O PSD garantiu que não repassou quantia maior do que a que recebeu do Fundo Eleitoral, e considera a possibilidade de o problema estar nas prestações de contas dos candidatos. O Podemos afirmou que deve analisar o caso mais detalhadamente, para entender o que pode ter acontecido.

Já o TSE informou que eventuais erros serão apurados pela justiça eleitoral no julgamento das contas dessas campanhas.

Para a advogada e contadora Blenda Fonseca, que atua na análise jurídica de prestações de contas eleitorais, informações incorretas, omissões ou divergências podem prejudicar a transparência e a correta identificação da origem e da destinação dos recursos de campanha. “Isso é especialmente relevante quando falamos do Fundo Eleitoral, que é composto por recursos públicos", disse.

Blenda pondera, porém, que nem toda divergência contábil configura uma irregularidade grave. Punições mais severas só ocorrem em alguns casos, quando a falha impede a identificação da origem dos recursos, compromete a comprovação de sua aplicação ou revela desvio de finalidade. "Entre as consequências para os candidatos está a desaprovação das contas e a determinação de devolução dos valores ao Tesouro Nacional", disse a especialista.

Dos seis partidos com divergências entre os valores declarados pelos candidatos e a verba recebida, a maior aparece no PP. A sigla recebeu R$ 417,07 milhões do Fundo Eleitoral, mas teve R$ 422,13 milhões registrados como repasses do diretório nacional, dos estaduais e do municipal, uma diferença de R$ 5,06 milhões.

Se considerados apenas os repasses do diretório nacional do PP, feitos diretamente para as candidaturas, os valores declarados ainda são maiores do que a verba recebida pela sigla, uma diferença de R$ 4,8 milhões. Isso não acontece nos outros cinco partidos.

No União Brasil, os valores repassados pelos diretórios nacionais, estaduais e municipais somam R$ 530,61 milhões, mas o partido recebeu R$ 526,24 milhões do Fundo eleitoral, uma diferença de R$ 4,36 milhões. Os repasses apenas do diretório nacional somam R$ 511,59 milhões.

No PSD, os candidatos declararam repasses de R$ 424,17 milhões, enquanto o partido recebeu R$ 421,01 milhões, uma diferença de R$ 3,16 milhões. Já no Podemos, a soma dos repasses declarados chega a R$ 247,76 milhões. A quantia é R$ 1,79 milhão a mais do que os R$ 245,97 milhões que a legenda recebeu.

As menores diferenças foram identificadas no Republicanos e no PCdoB. No primeiro, os candidatos declararam R$ 348,81 milhões em repasses, enquanto a legenda recebeu R$ 348,59 milhões, uma diferença de R$ 220,5 mil. Já no PCdoB, foram declarados R$ 60,66 milhões, quase R$ 128 mil a mais do que os R$ 60,53 milhões recebidos pela legenda.

PL e PRTB têm repasses declarados abaixo de 30% para mulheres e negros

O levantamento também identificou diferenças na proporção de recursos do Fundo Eleitoral declarados como recebidos por candidaturas femininas e de pessoas negras. PL e PRTB são os únicos que aparecem abaixo de 30% nas duas categorias.

🔎Pelas regras eleitorais, os partidos devem destinar às campanhas femininas recursos do FEFC em proporção correspondente à participação das mulheres no total de candidaturas, respeitado o mínimo de 30%. Para candidaturas de pessoas negras, consideradas as pessoas pretas e pardas, a Emenda Constitucional nº 133/2024 estabeleceu um piso de 30% dos recursos eleitorais. As regras também contemplam a distribuição de recursos para candidaturas indígenas.

No PL, os valores declarados como destinados a candidaturas femininas somam R$ 225,8 milhões, equivalentes a 25,90% do total de R$ 871,8 milhões atribuído aos repasses dos diretórios nacionais e estaduais. Já as candidaturas de pessoas pretas e pardas declararam ter recebido R$ 192,9 milhões, o equivalente a 22,12% desse montante.

Procurado pelo g1 , o partido não respondeu.

No PRTB, apenas candidaturas masculinas declaram repasses do Fundo Eleitoral. Pelas candidaturas negras, foram declarados R$ 298,5 mil, equivalentes a 14,08% dos R$ 2,1 milhões informados como repasses dos diretórios nacionais e estaduais.

O partido enfrenta uma disputa interna pelo comando nacional da legenda, envolvendo grupos ligados a Leonardo Avalanche, que ocupa a presidência atualmente, e Amauri Pinho, que estava no cargo, mas teve que sair por causa uma decisão judicial favorável a Avalanche.

Pinho questionou a destinação dos recursos e defendeu uma auditoria independente no partido. “Os dados apresentados apontam repasses abaixo do mínimo exigido para mulheres e candidatos negros, além de indícios de possível desvio de cerca de R$ 2 milhões do Fundo Eleitoral sob a gestão de Leonardo Avalanche. Ele deve esclarecer a destinação desses recursos”, afirmou.

A atual administração do PRTB foi procurada, mas não respondeu.

Segundo a cientista política Beatriz Mendes, pesquisadora da Universidade de São Paulo (USP), os critérios adotados pelos partidos para selecionar as campanhas que receberão mais dinheiro podem reproduzir desigualdades já existentes. "Os efeitos ultrapassam o resultado individual das candidaturas e alcançam a composição dos espaços de decisão política", afirmou.

STF analisa anistia a partidos que descumpriram cotas

Os percentuais abaixo de 30% não permitem afirmar que o PL e o PRTB descumpriram as cotas eleitorais. Isso porque o levantamento se baseia nas receitas informadas pelos candidatos. Segundo a advogada Bianca Gonçalves e Silva, a Justiça Eleitoral verifica o cumprimento das cotas a partir das prestações de contas anuais dos partidos, cujo julgamento leva cerca de dois anos.

Além disso, os partidos têm conseguido anistias das punições por descumprimento das cotas raciais e de gênero em eleições anteriores, por meio de mecanismos como um dispositivo da Emenda Constitucional nº 117/2022.

O julgamento de uma ação que questiona a validades das anistias teve início no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) em 11 de março de 2026, sob relatoria do ministro Gilmar Mendes, mas foi suspenso.

Para Bianca Gonçalves e Silva, livrar os partidos das punições enfraquece a efetividade das ações afirmativas destinadas a ampliar a participação política de mulheres e pessoas negras. “O perigo dessas anistias é exatamente fazer os partidos não cumprirem a obrigação. Vira uma letra morta, que não tem efetividade”, afirmou.

A pesquisadora avalia que os partidos atuam politicamente para afastar as consequências de irregularidades. “A maioria dos dirigentes partidários são parlamentares. Então, eles estão legislando em causa própria”, disse a advogada.
